title: Why Focusing On Details Is Effective Teaching
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Asked what single piece of advice he would give teachers, Linsin identifies one common mistake: failing to teach lessons, routines, and expectations with enough detail. He argues that most teachers stop short of the granular, explicit instruction needed to actually get students to meet high expectations, and that highly detailed teaching is the practical answer to the abstract call for rigor. He explains several ways this benefits students: it provides a clear roadmap that eliminates confusion, builds confidence by making difficult material achievable, and—contrary to teacher assumptions—captures genuine student interest better than broad conceptual overviews. Detail-oriented teaching also fosters independent, tenacious work and instills a transferable habit of attentiveness. Linsin ties it all together by arguing that detailed teaching produces intrinsic motivation, since doing something well feels good and makes students want more of that feeling, which in turn keeps them engaged and away from misbehavior.
points: Most teachers under-teach details; going deeper into the granular "how" is what actually helps students meet high expectations.
Detailed instruction provides a clear roadmap, eliminating student confusion about what success requires.
Contrary to common assumption, details generate more student interest and fascination than broad conceptual overviews.
Detail-focused teaching builds independence, tenacious work habits, and a transferable habit of attentiveness.
Highly detailed teaching produces genuine intrinsic motivation because doing something well feels good and creates a desire for more.
quotes: The mistake is this: Failing to teach lessons, routines, rules, and expectations—or anything else for that matter—with enough detail.
Most teachers I observe tend to focus on the big picture. They linger on broad conceptual whats and whys because they assume that smaller, fact-heavy details are boring. But the opposite is true.
Details best prepare students to perform independently because they remove all fears, concerns, and questions over what, specifically, they need to do to succeed.
Highly detailed teaching develops strong intrinsic motivation.
So shine a light into every crook and cranny. Bridge every gap with incremental stepping stones.
